providers.description: Client providers contributed by modules, outermost first.

body-end.description: Components rendered at the end of <body> (analytics, consent banners, toasters).

header-actions.description: Components rendered in the site header next to the theme toggle (sign-in, cart …).

next-plugins.description: next.config wrappers (Sentry, next-intl …). Generated into src/generated/next.ts.

proxy.type: (request: NextRequest, response: NextResponse) => Response | undefined | Promise<Response | undefined>
proxy.description: Request handlers run by src/proxy.ts in order. Set cookies/headers on `response` and return nothing to continue, or return a Response to stop.

html-lang.description: Resolvers for <html lang> (i18n). The first non-empty result wins; otherwise site.config.ts locale.

error-reporters.description: Called by error.tsx and global-error.tsx with errors caught by React boundaries (Sentry …). Client-side.

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL
env.description: Canonical public URL of the site, no trailing slash. Falls back to the url in site.config.ts

seo.name: seo
seo.title: SEO
seo.description: sitemap.xml, robots.txt (no-index outside production), JSON-LD helpers and generated Open Graph images.

sitemap.description: Functions returning sitemap entries (blog posts, docs pages …), merged into /sitemap.xml.

postInstall: robots.txt blocks indexing unless VERCEL_ENV=production (or NODE_ENV=production off Vercel).
Open Graph images use colors from src/lib/seo/og-theme.ts.

analytics.name: analytics
analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: One track() for Plausible, PostHog, Google Analytics 4 or Umami, chosen by env vars; waits for cookie consent when the provider needs it; logs events locally in dev.

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN
env.description: Enables Plausible (cookieless) for this domain

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAUSIBLE_SRC
env.description: Script URL for self-hosted Plausible (default https://plausible.io/js/script.js)

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY
env.description: Enables PostHog (project API key, phc_…)
env.howTo: PostHog → Project settings → Project API key

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST
env.description: PostHog ingest host

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID
env.description: Enables Google Analytics 4 (G-XXXXXXX)

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID
env.description: Enables Umami (cookieless)

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_UMAMI_SRC
env.description: Umami script URL (default Umami Cloud)

postInstall: Set the env var for one provider (e.g. NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN). Without any, track() logs to the browser console in development.
Custom events: import { track } from "@/lib/analytics/track"; track("signup", { plan: "pro" }).

ci.name: ci
ci.title: GitHub Actions CI
ci.description: Lint, typecheck, test and build on every push and pull request, with cached installs and Next.js builds, least-privilege tokens and grouped Dependabot updates.
postInstall: Push to GitHub: CI runs on pushes to main and on every pull request.

vercel.name: vercel
vercel.title: Vercel deployment
vercel.description: vercel.json that checks production env vars before building, security-minded defaults, and a step-by-step deploy guide.
postInstall: Import the repository at vercel.com/new, add the variables from .env.example, and deploy.

cookie-consent.name: cookie-consent
cookie-consent.title: Cookie consent
cookie-consent.description: GDPR-style consent banner with equal accept/reject, per-category choices, and a cookie contract other modules read.

cookieConsent.title: Cookies
cookieConsent.description: We use essential cookies to run this site, and optional ones to understand usage and improve it. You choose.

postInstall: Consent is stored in the `site_consent` cookie ({"v":1,"analytics":bool,"marketing":bool}).
Any link to #cookie-settings reopens the banner (one is added to the legal footer links).

mdx.name: mdx
mdx.title: MDX content
mdx.description: Typed MDX collections: Zod-validated frontmatter, drafts, TOC, reading time, token-themed code highlighting, RSS helper.
postInstall: Content lives in /content. Define a collection with defineCollection({ directory, schema }).
Code highlighting is driven by theme tokens (primary, success, warning, ring): no extra CSS.

legal.name: legal
legal.title: Legal pages
legal.description: Privacy policy, terms of service and cookie policy as editable MDX templates filled from site.config.
postInstall: Fill the `legal` block in site.config.ts: the templates use those values.
The templates are a starting point, not legal advice. Have them reviewed for your jurisdiction.

email.name: email
email.title: Email
email.description: Send React Email templates through Resend. In development, mail lands in a local outbox at /dev/outbox.

env.name: RESEND_API_KEY
env.description: Resend API key. Without it (in development) emails are saved to the local outbox

env.name: EMAIL_FROM
env.description: Default sender, on a domain verified in Resend

env.name: EMAIL_OUTBOX
env.description: Set to 1 to capture every email in the outbox instead of sending (previews, staging, CI). /dev/outbox then works in production builds too

postInstall: In development, open /dev/outbox to read every email the site sends.
For production, verify your domain in Resend and set RESEND_API_KEY + EMAIL_FROM.
Email colors live in src/emails/theme.ts (email clients can't read CSS variables).

rate-limit.name: rate-limit
rate-limit.title: Rate limiting
rate-limit.description: Sliding-window rate limits for actions and API routes. Upstash Redis in production, in-memory locally.

env.name: UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL
env.description: Upstash Redis REST URL. Without it, limits are kept in memory (per server instance)

env.name: UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN
env.description: Upstash Redis REST token

contact.name: contact
contact.title: Contact form
contact.description: Contact page and form with layered spam protection (honeypot, timing, rate limit, optional Turnstile) and email delivery.

env.name: CONTACT_TO_EMAIL
env.description: Inbox that receives contact form submissions

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY
env.description: Cloudflare Turnstile site key. Set both Turnstile keys to add an invisible challenge

env.name: TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY
env.description: Cloudflare Turnstile secret key

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.description: Questions, ideas or feedback. We read every message and reply by email.
contact.successMessage: Thanks! Your message is on its way. We'll get back to you by email.

postInstall: Set CONTACT_TO_EMAIL to the inbox that should receive messages.
Page copy lives in site.config.ts under `contact`.
Optional: add Cloudflare Turnstile keys for an invisible bot challenge.

blog.name: blog
blog.title: Blog
blog.description: MDX blog with static pagination, tags, reading time, per-post OG images, RSS, JSON-LD and sitemap entries.
postInstall: Write posts in content/blog/*.mdx. Frontmatter: title, date, description?, tags?, image?, draft?
Delete content/blog/welcome.mdx once you have a real post.

changelog.name: changelog
changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.description: Release notes from MDX: dated entries with versions and change types, deep links, RSS feed.
postInstall: Add entries as content/changelog/<date>-<slug>.mdx with title, date, version? and type?.

faq.name: faq
faq.title: FAQ
faq.description: Typed FAQ data source (content/faq.json) grouped by category, a /faq page and FAQPage structured data.
postInstall: Edit content/faq.json. Use getFaqs() with the faq section on any page (e.g. pricing).

database.name: database
database.title: Database
database.description: Drizzle ORM on Postgres (Neon, Supabase or any Postgres). Zero-setup embedded PGlite in development with automatic schema push.

env.name: DATABASE_URL
env.description: Postgres connection string. Unset in development = embedded PGlite in .site/dev/pglite
env.howTo: Neon: console.neon.tech → Connection string (pooled). Supabase: Project settings → Database → Transaction pooler

postInstall: Development needs nothing: `pnpm dev` pushes the schema into an embedded PGlite database.
Production: set DATABASE_URL, then `pnpm db:generate` and `pnpm db:migrate` (commit the /drizzle folder).

auth.name: auth
auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: Better Auth: email + password with verification, magic links, Google and GitHub OAuth, password reset, protected routes.

env.name: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
env.description: Secret for signing sessions and tokens (32+ random characters)

env.name: BETTER_AUTH_URL
env.description: Public base URL for auth callbacks. Defaults to the site URL in production and the request origin in development

env.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
env.description: Google OAuth client ID (enables “Continue with Google”)
env.howTo: console.cloud.google.com → APIs & Services → Credentials; redirect URI: <site>/api/auth/callback/google

env.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: Google OAuth client secret

env.name: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID
env.description: GitHub OAuth app client ID (enables “Continue with GitHub”)

env.name: GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: GitHub OAuth app client secret

auth-plugins.description: Better Auth server plugins contributed by modules (teams → organization, admin → admin).

auth-client-plugins.description: Better Auth client plugins matching the server plugins.

auth-events.description: Handlers for user lifecycle events (welcome email, notifications, onboarding).

postInstall: Development works immediately: verification and magic-link emails land in /dev/outbox.
Production: set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET; add Google/GitHub credentials to show their buttons.
Protect a page with `await requireSession()` from @/lib/auth/session (the proxy also redirects protectedPaths).

dashboard.name: dashboard
dashboard.title: Dashboard shell
dashboard.description: Signed-in app area: sidebar + topbar layout, nav from site.config, overview with widget and topbar slots for other modules.

dashboard-widgets.description: Cards on the dashboard overview (plan, team, notifications …). Server components.

dashboard-topbar.description: Items in the app top bar (team switcher, notifications …). Server components.

postInstall: Build your app under src/app/(app)/: every page there gets the shell and requires a session.
Add sidebar links in site.config.ts → nav.dashboard (icon names from lucide, e.g. "bar-chart-3").

settings.name: settings
settings.title: Profile & settings
settings.description: Account settings: profile, email change, password, active sessions with revoke, account deletion. Tabs other modules extend.
postInstall: Other modules add tabs through nav.settings (billing, team, API keys, notifications).

payments.name: payments
payments.title: Payments
payments.description: Provider-agnostic checkout, customer portal and webhooks (Stripe adapter), with a mock provider so billing works locally with zero keys.

env.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
env.description: Stripe secret key. Unset in development = mock provider with a fake checkout at /dev/checkout

env.name: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.description: Signing secret of the webhook endpoint <site>/api/payments/webhook
env.howTo: Dashboard → Developers → Webhooks, or `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/payments/webhook`

payment-webhooks.description: Handlers for normalized payment events (billing → subscriptions, store → orders).

postInstall: Development: no keys needed. Checkouts open a mock payment page at /dev/checkout.
Production: set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET; subscribe the webhook to checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.* and invoice.payment_failed.

billing.name: billing
billing.title: Billing
billing.description: Subscriptions from plans in site.config: pricing page, checkout, webhooks, customer portal, entitlements and limits.
postInstall: Plans, prices, features and limits live in site.config.ts → billing.plans.
Development: checkout uses the mock provider (/dev/checkout). Production: `pnpm billing:sync` creates the Stripe products and prices (lookup keys <plan>_monthly / <plan>_yearly).

teams.name: teams
teams.title: Teams
teams.description: Organizations with roles (owner, admin, member), email invitations, team switcher and team settings, on Better Auth's organization plugin.
postInstall: Create a team from the switcher in the top bar. Invitations are emailed (see /dev/outbox in development).

admin.name: admin
admin.title: Admin panel
admin.description: Admin area on Better Auth's admin plugin: user search, roles, ban/unban, session revocation, impersonation with a stop banner.

env.name: ADMIN_EMAILS
env.description: Comma-separated emails that are promoted to admin the first time they open /admin

postInstall: Make yourself admin: set ADMIN_EMAILS=you@example.com, or run `pnpm admin:grant you@example.com`.
Non-admins get a 404 at /admin (the area's existence isn't revealed).

notifications.name: notifications
notifications.title: In-app notifications
notifications.description: Notification inbox: notify(userId, …) from anywhere, a bell with unread count in the top bar, and a /notifications page.
postInstall: Send one from any server code: await notify(user.id, { title: "Export ready", href: "/exports/42" }).

transactional-emails.name: transactional-emails
transactional-emails.title: Transactional emails
transactional-emails.description: Welcome email after verification, plus /dev/emails: a gallery previewing every email template installed by any module.

email-templates.description: Email templates (with PreviewProps) shown in the /dev/emails gallery.

postInstall: Open /dev/emails in development to preview every template with sample data.

onboarding.name: onboarding
onboarding.title: Onboarding
onboarding.description: A focused first-run questionnaire configured in site.config.ts, plus a setup checklist on the dashboard that other modules add tasks to.

onboarding-tasks.description: Setup checklist items on the dashboard (choose a plan, invite a teammate …), each with a done(userId) check.

questions.title: How many people will use it?
What do you want to get done first?
questions.placeholder: e.g. launch our beta by June

postInstall: Edit the questions in site.config.ts → onboarding.questions; read answers with getOnboardingAnswers(userId).
Modules add checklist items through the onboarding-tasks slot; add your own in src/lib/onboarding/state.ts.

api.name: api
api.title: Public API
api.description: Hashed API keys with scopes and expiry, an apiRoute() helper (auth, Zod validation, rate limits, problem+json errors), /api/v1/me and an API keys settings tab.
postInstall: Create a key at /settings/api-keys, then: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" <site>/api/v1/me
New endpoint: export const GET = apiRoute({ scope: "read" }, async ({ principal }) => ({ … })) in src/app/api/v1/<name>/route.ts.

docs.name: docs
docs.title: Docs
docs.description: Documentation from MDX folders: sidebar, prev/next, TOC, edit links and ⌘K client-side search (static index, lazy-loaded).
postInstall: Pages live in content/docs. Folders become sidebar groups; `order` in frontmatter sorts pages.
Set docs.editUrl in site.config.ts (e.g. https://github.com/you/repo/edit/main/) for edit links.

alert.name: alert
alert.description: Inline message for info, success, warning and errors, announced to screen readers.

avatar.name: avatar
avatar.description: Image avatar with initials fallback while loading or on error.

badge.name: badge
badge.description: Small status label with neutral, outline and semantic variants.

button.name: button
button.description: Button with variants and sizes; renders any element via asChild (links, triggers).

card.name: card
card.description: Surface for grouped content: header, title, description, content, footer.

checkbox.name: checkbox
checkbox.description: Accessible checkbox (Radix) that submits with native forms.

copy-button.name: copy-button
copy-button.description: Button that copies a value to the clipboard and confirms it, announced to screen readers.

dialog.name: dialog
dialog.description: Modal dialog (Radix): focus trap, Esc to close, scroll lock.

dropdown-menu.name: dropdown-menu
dropdown-menu.description: Menu with keyboard navigation, checkable items and sub-menus (Radix).

field.name: field
field.description: Accessible form field: wires label, description and error to any control via ids.

input.name: input
input.description: Text input styled with tokens; supports aria-invalid and file inputs.

label.name: label
label.description: Native form label (no client JS) that dims with a disabled peer.

native-select.name: native-select
native-select.description: Styled native <select>: zero JS, best mobile UX, works in any form.

popover.name: popover
popover.description: Floating panel anchored to a trigger (Radix).

progress.name: progress
progress.description: Accessible progress bar (role=progressbar) with value and label.

prose.name: prose
prose.description: Typography for rendered Markdown/MDX, fully driven by theme tokens.

separator.name: separator
separator.description: Horizontal or vertical divider with correct separator semantics.

switch.name: switch
switch.description: On/off toggle (Radix) that submits with native forms.

table.name: table
table.description: Responsive data table parts with horizontal scrolling on small screens.

textarea.name: textarea
textarea.description: Multi-line text input that grows with its content where supported.

auth-card.name: auth-card
auth-card.title: Auth screen
auth-card.description: Centered or split-screen frame for sign-in, sign-up and reset flows.

blog-list.name: blog-list
blog-list.title: Blog list
blog-list.description: Post cards as a grid or a compact list, with dates, tags and reading time.

cta-band.name: cta-band
cta-band.title: CTA band
cta-band.description: Closing call to action; inverted, muted or bordered.

dashboard-shell.name: dashboard-shell
dashboard-shell.title: Dashboard shell
dashboard-shell.description: App layout: sidebar nav with active state, topbar, mobile drawer via the Popover API.

empty-state.name: empty-state
empty-state.title: Empty state
empty-state.description: Icon, message and next actions for empty lists and first-run screens.

faq.name: faq
faq.title: FAQ
faq.description: Questions as native <details> (exclusive, zero JS), with optional side intro.

feature-grid.name: feature-grid
feature-grid.title: Feature grid
feature-grid.description: 2–4 column grid of features with icons and optional links.

feature-rows.name: feature-rows
feature-rows.title: Feature rows
feature-rows.description: Alternating media/text rows with bullets and actions.

hero-centered.name: hero-centered
hero-centered.title: Hero: centered
hero-centered.description: Centered headline, lead, actions and optional media below.

page-header.name: page-header
page-header.title: Page header
page-header.description: Title block for inner pages with eyebrow, description, breadcrumbs and actions.

pricing-table.name: pricing-table
pricing-table.title: Pricing table
pricing-table.description: Plans with monthly/yearly toggle (CSS-only, no JS), features and CTAs. Reads plans from config.

section-kit.name: section-kit
section-kit.title: Section kit
section-kit.description: Shared building blocks for every section: Section wrapper with tones, SectionHeader, actions, media types.

testimonials.name: testimonials
testimonials.title: Testimonials
testimonials.description: Quote cards in a masonry-like grid, with an optional featured quote.
